question.text: Ms. Arushi Bhatia holds 5% in 'Priya Foods Pvt Ltd'. 'Lotus Ventures' Cat II AIF holds ROFR over her shares. Arushi receives a market offer of INR 500/share from a third party. Lotus Ventures is willing to pay INR 450. Under ROFR:

answer.text: Arushi must sell to Lotus at INR 450 since Lotus holds ROFR
Lotus has a veto and can block the entire sale
Arushi can freely sell to the third party at INR 500 without any offer to Lotus
Arushi must offer the shares to Lotus at INR 500 (the best market quote); if Lotus matches, it buys; if Lotus refuses, Arushi sells to the third party at INR 500

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Ch 11.6.6, under ROFR, the selling shareholder must approach the ROFR-holder with the BEST market quote. The ROFR-holder either MATCHES that quote and buys, or refuses. Arushi cannot sell below the offered price to the third party if Lotus is willing to match. Lotus does not get to set a lower price (that's not ROFR). The Trap: Option A describes a call-option style right, not ROFR. Option C ignores ROFR altogether. Option D describes veto right, not ROFR. Cross-Exam Context: Same ROFR arithmetic across XIX-A, XIX-C, and XV (M&A scenarios). Manager's Pro-Tip: ROFR exercise must be documented with the third-party offer on record. Without the paper trail, disputes arise as to whether the 'matched quote' was genuine.
